|url-status=live }}</ref> The film was certified by the Korean and [[Kijkwijzer|Dutch ratings board]] prior to its release, the former reporting that it was 5 hours and 12 minutes in length.<ref name="telegraph speculation"/> On 19 December 2018, Netflix added the title ''Black Mirror: Bandersnatch'' as an upcoming film, with the tagline "Be right back", in reference to the earlier episode of [[Be Right Back|the same name]]. Various runtimes including 2 minutes, 36 minutes and 90 minutes were listed in different territories.<ref name="telegraph speculation"/> In late December, media reported on an image of the cast and a claim that Slade would direct the episode.<ref name="indy speculation">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-film-cast-fionn-whitehead-will-poulter-asim-chaudhry-release-a8698826.html |title=Black Mirror film 'Bandersnatch' cast confirmed in new photo |work=[[The Independent]] |last=Stolworthy |first=Jacob |date=25 December 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225195523/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-film-cast-fionn-whitehead-will-poulter-asim-chaudhry-release-a8698826.html |archive-date=25 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="telegraph speculation">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/0/bandersnatch-solving-riddle-black-mirrors-secret-christmas-episode/ |title=What is Bandersnatch? Solving the riddle of Black Mirror's secret Christmas episode |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |last=Vincent |first=Alice |date=20 December 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |url-access=limited |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224031501/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/0/bandersnatch-solving-riddle-black-mirrors-secret-christmas-episode/ |archive-date=24 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-movie-details-five-hours-footage-1202030410/ |title='Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Page Goes Live on Netflix and It's a Movie, Reportedly Has Five Hours of Footage |work=[[IndieWire]] |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=24 December 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224234714/https://www.indiewire.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-movie-details-five-hours-footage-1202030410/ |archive-date=24 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The interactive nature of ''Bandersnatch'' was first publicly mentioned by [[Bloomberg News]] in October 2018, which cited an unnamed source that Netflix was developing an interactive episode of ''Black Mirror'' alongside several other interactive specials for release in 2018.<ref name="bloomberg">{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-10-01/netflix-is-said-to-plan-choose-your-own-adventure-black-mirror |title=Netflix Is Planning a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure 'Black Mirror' |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |publisher=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=1 October 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225115319/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-10-01/netflix-is-said-to-plan-choose-your-own-adventure-black-mirror |archive-date=25 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> A Netflix spokesperson, when asked by ''[[The Verge]]'', responded with: "Thanks for reaching out! You have the ability to choose your own response from Netflix: this or this." The first "this" contained a link to a GIF from ''[[Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt]]'' of a character saying "razzmatazz", and the second linking to a YouTube video of crickets chirping.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/1/17923978/netflix-interactive-episode-black-mirror-season-5-release-date-2018-charlie-booker |title=Netflix will reportedly release an interactive Black Mirror episode in 2018 |work=[[The Verge]] |last=Robinson |first=Tasha |date=1 October 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181213162757/https://www.theverge.com/2018/10/1/17923978/netflix-interactive-episode-black-mirror-season-5-release-date-2018-charlie-booker |archive-date=13 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> No [[screener (promotional)|screeners]] were sent to critics in advance of the film's release, though Netflix invited select media writers to their headquarters about a month prior to release and gave them an opportunity to try the interactive film.<ref name="thr"/>

Only upon the film's release on 28 December did Netflix publicly confirm its interactive nature. Carla Engelbrecht, Netflix's director of product innovation, told ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' that they did not officially announce that ''Bandersnatch'' would be an interactive episode so that viewers would not have "preconceived notions", such as an overestimation of the level of interactivity.<ref name="thr"/> Due to unpleasant comments following the release of ''Bandersnatch'', Poulter announced that he would reduce his [[Twitter]] activity for mental health reasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-bandersnatch-star-will-poulter-leaves-twitter-1172742|title='Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Star Will Poulter Leaves Twitter Amid Backlash|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Strause|first=Jackie|date=3 January 2019|access-date=3 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103193633/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-bandersnatch-star-will-poulter-leaves-twitter-1172742|archive-date=3 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> In a November 2021 interview with ''[[GQ (magazine)|GQ]]'', Poulter stated that he deleted his Twitter account in January 2019 after being [[Cyberbullying|harassed]] by [[wiktionary:keyboard warrior|keyboard warriors]] who mocked his appearance as Ritman. Poulter returned to Twitter in 2021, but he now uses it for platform causes that he supports like [[The Black Curriculum]] and [[Alzheimer's Research UK]].<ref name="PoulterGQ">{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Ben |date=November 11, 2021 |title=Will Poulter: 'I'm very honoured to have been welcomed into the Marvel family' |url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/culture/article/will-poulter-guardians-of-the-galaxy-3-interview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117201432/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/culture/article/will-poulter-guardians-of-the-galaxy-3-interview |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |access-date=November 22, 2021 |website=[[GQ]]}}</ref>

A week following the film's premiere, Netflix sent out a hint on its social media pages directing users on how to discover an obscure scene.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.avclub.com/netflix-is-out-here-goosing-people-into-finding-weird-b-1831611911 | title = Netflix is out here goosing people into finding weird Bandersnatch endings | first = Dan | last = Neilan | date = 9 January 2019 | access-date = 9 January 2019 | work = [[The A.V. Club]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190110010405/https://news.avclub.com/netflix-is-out-here-goosing-people-into-finding-weird-b-1831611911 | archive-date = 10 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref> A week later, Netflix tweeted pieces of data about viewer choices in the episode. For instance, 73% of viewers chose for Stefan to initially accept the job at Tuckersoft and of what Netflix deemed to be the five endings, the least viewed was the one where Stefan boards the train with his mother as a child.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a25943238/netflix-black-mirror-bandersnatch-endings-least-popular/|title=Netflix reveals Black Mirror: Bandersnatch's least chosen ending|work=[[Digital Spy]]|last=Houghton|first=Rianne|date=18 January 2019|access-date=20 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119212328/https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a25943238/netflix-black-mirror-bandersnatch-endings-least-popular/|archive-date=19 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Later, Netflix reported that 94% of viewers were actively making choices.<ref name="thr may2019"/>

Following the release of ''Bandersnatch'' to Netflix, a live website for the fictional company Tuckersoft was made available. The site documented some of the fictional games discussed in the film and included a playable version of ''Nohzdyve'' that required the use of a [[ZX Spectrum]] computer or an emulator.<ref name="verge game"/> The film was also advertised after its release on the [[London Underground]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/bandersnatch-poster-london-underground-2425700|title=This creepy 'Bandersnatch' poster was spotted on the London Underground|work=[[NME]]|last=Maine|first=Samantha|date=1 January 2019|access-date=20 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711201442/https://www.nme.com/news/tv/bandersnatch-poster-london-underground-2425700|archive-date=11 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Within a week of its release, a number of mock "Tucker's Newsagent and Games" storefronts appeared in London and Birmingham, styled as a 1980s store with the various Tuckersoft games, and [[VHS]] tapes of other ''Black Mirror'' episodes.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.tvguide.com/news/black-mirror-bandersnatch-pop-up-stores-easter-eggs/ | title = Black Mirror: Bandersnatch Takes Meta to the Next Level With Pop-Up Stores | first = Amanda | last = Bell | date = 6 January 2019 | access-date = 6 January 2019 | work = [[TV Guide]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190106210329/https://www.tvguide.com/news/black-mirror-bandersnatch-pop-up-stores-easter-eggs/ | archive-date = 6 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/black-mirror-comes-to-life-as-bandersnatch-pop-up-appears-at-londons-old-street-station-2426445|title='Black Mirror' comes to life as 'Bandersnatch' pop-up appears at London's Old Street station|work=[[NME]]|last=Reilly|first=Nick|date=3 January 2019|access-date=20 June 2020|archive-date=21 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421155454/https://www.nme.com/news/black-mirror-comes-to-life-as-bandersnatch-pop-up-appears-at-londons-old-street-station-2426445|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Netflix and interactive fiction==
Netflix had previously released interactive programmes for children, starting in 2017 with ''[[Puss in Book]]''.<ref name="bloomberg"/> Netflix also released the 2015 [[Telltale Games]] interactive series ''[[Minecraft: Story Mode]]'' on their website in November 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ign.com/articles/2018/11/27/telltales-minecraft-story-mode-launches-on-netflix |title=Telltale's Minecraft: Story Mode Launches on Netflix |work=[[IGN]] |last=Stevens |first=Colin |date=27 December 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181128165803/https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/11/27/telltales-minecraft-story-mode-launches-on-netflix |archive-date=28 November 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Bandersnatch'' was their first release targeted at adults.<ref name="variety interview"/> Netflix went on to produce additional shows using the Branch Manager tool. [[Bear Grylls]]'s eight-episode interactive reality series ''[[You vs. Wild]]'', fashioned after ''[[Man vs. Wild]]'', was released in April 2019. An interactive special for the comedy ''Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt, [[Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt: Kimmy vs the Reverend|Kimmy vs the Reverend]],'' was released in May 2020.<ref name="thr may2019"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/behind-screen/netflix-sets-live-action-interactive-series-you-wild-bear-grylls-1195401|title=Netflix Sets Live-Action Interactive Series 'You vs. Wild'|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Giardina|first=Carolyn|date=18 March 2019|access-date=18 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331075813/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/behind-screen/netflix-sets-live-action-interactive-series-you-wild-bear-grylls-1195401|archive-date=31 March 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/netflix-takes-a-crack-at-interactive-comedy-unbreakable-kimmy-schmidt-special-1293377|title=Netflix Takes a Crack at Interactive Comedy With 'Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt' Special|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Beresford|first=Trilby|date=11 May 2020|access-date=18 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514105544/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/netflix-takes-a-crack-at-interactive-comedy-unbreakable-kimmy-schmidt-special-1293377|archive-date=14 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

''The Verge''{{'s}} [[Jesse Damiani]] commented that interactivity as in ''Bandersnatch'' could potentially be used by Netflix to collect user-preference data and inform marketing choices, such as targeted product placement.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/2019/1/2/18165182/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-interactive-strategy-marketing | title = Black Mirror: Bandersnatch Could Become Netflix's Secret Marketing Weapon | first = Jesse | last = Damiani | date = 2 January 2018 | access-date = 2 January 2018 | work = [[The Verge]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190102202148/https://www.theverge.com/2019/1/2/18165182/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-interactive-strategy-marketing | archive-date = 2 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref> In February, technology policy researcher [[Michael Veale]] requested the data that Netflix stored about his viewings of ''Bandersnatch'' under the [[General Data Protection Regulation]]. He criticised that the data, detailing every choice he had made, was not anonymised and was taken without explicit consent from the user.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/2/13/18223071/netflix-bandersnatch-gdpr-request-choice-data|title=Netflix records all of your Bandersnatch choices, GDPR request reveals|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=13 February 2019|website=[[The Verge]]|access-date=16 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214145809/https://www.theverge.com/2019/2/13/18223071/netflix-bandersnatch-gdpr-request-choice-data|archive-date=14 February 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/netflix-has-saved-every-choice-youve-ever-made-in-black-mirror-bandersnatch/|title=Netflix Has Saved Every Choice You've Ever Made in 'Black Mirror: Bandersnatch'|last1=Gault|first1=Matthew|last2=Koebler|first2=Jason|date=12 February 2019|website=[[Motherboard (website)|Motherboard]]|language=en-US|access-date=16 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215132041/https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/article/j57gkk/netflix-has-saved-every-choice-youve-ever-made-in-black-mirror-bandersnatch|archive-date=15 February 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> A 2019 paper by researchers at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] demonstrated how to infer viewers' choices in ''Bandersnatch'' through network packet analysis with 96% accuracy. The paper noted that this could be used to reveal viewer preferences "from benign (e.g., their food and music preferences) to sensitive (e.g., their affinity to violence and political inclination)", and noted a technical solution Netflix could implement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2019/03/19/netflix_privacy_hole/|title=Bandersnatch to gander snatched: Black Mirror choices can be snooped on, thanks to privacy-leaking Netflix streams|work=[[The Register]]|last=Claburn|first=Thomas|date=19 March 2019|access-date=21 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190320150631/https://www.theregister.co.uk/2019/03/19/netflix_privacy_hole/|archive-date=20 March 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Mitra|first1=Gargi|last2=Vairam|first2=Prasanna Karthik|last3=SLPSK|first3=Patanjali|last4=Chandrachoodan|first4=Nitin|last5=V|first5=Kamakoti|date=2019|title=Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2019 Conference Posters and Demos|chapter=White Mirror |pages=122–124 |doi=10.1145/3342280.3342330 |arxiv=1903.06475|isbn=9781450368865 |s2cid=80628336 }}</ref>

As Netflix moved into more traditional gaming markets in the early 2020s, the company’s development and output of interactive programmes slowed, with then-vice president of Netflix Games Mike Verdu stating in an interview in December 2023 that “the technology was very limiting and the potential for what we could do in that realm was kind of capped” and said that Netflix were “not building those specific experiences anymore”.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Totilo |first=Stephen |date=8 January 2024 |title=Source: Xbox has considered bringing hit Sea of Thieves to PlayStation |url=https://www.gamefile.news/p/sea-of-thieves-playstation |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=Game File |language=en}}</ref> Netflix later announced on 4 November 2024 that they would be removing most of their interactive programmes from the service the following month, though ''Bandersnatch'' would be one of the four interactive programmes that remained on the service.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jay |date=2024-11-04 |title=Netflix is removing nearly all of its interactive titles |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/11/4/24287857/netflix-removing-interactive-titles-games |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref> Game designer [[Sam Barlow (game designer)|Sam Barlow]], who had developed video games with [[full-motion video]] previously, said that ''Bandersnatch'' only worked as its story worked at a [[metafiction]] level with the nature of interactive works, a formula that couldn't easily be replicated in Netflix's future works.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/q-and-a/510794/sam-barlow-justin-mcelroy-netflix | title = Netflix revived and killed the interactive movie — but its platform is still a game | first = Simone | last = de Rochefort | date = January 19, 2025 | accessdate = January 19, 2025 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] }}</ref> Ahead of a major user-interface update removing 
interactive content functionality from its television apps, Netflix announced it would be pulling the last two interactive works, ''Bandersnatch'' and ''Kimmy vs the Reverend'', from the service in May 2025, with neither being made available in a linear format since.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/leaving-soon/black-mirror-bandersnatch-and-unbreakable-kimmy-schmidt-interactive-specials-leaving-netflix/ | title = 'Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' and 'Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt' Interactive Specials Leaving Netflix | first=  Kasey | last = Moore | date = 6 May 2025 | accessdate = 8 May 2025 | work = What's on Netflix }}</ref>

===Lawsuit===
[[Chooseco]], the company founded by [[R. A. Montgomery]] to republish the ''[[Choose Your Own Adventure]]'' book series, filed a lawsuit against Netflix for trademark infringement by use of the phrase "choose your own adventure" in ''Bandersnatch'', seeking upwards of {{USD|25 million|link=yes}} in damages. Chooseco claimed it trademarked the phrase in association with movies, books, and other forms of media, and that Netflix started negotiations with Chooseco in 2016 to license the phrase for films and animated series, which did not pan out.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://deadline.com/2019/01/netflixs-black-mirror-bandersnatch-subject-of-suit-over-use-of-choose-your-own-adventure-1202533643/ | title = Netflix's 'Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Sued Over Use Of "Choose Your Own Adventure" | first = Dawn | last = Chmielewski | date = 11 January 2019 | access-date = 11 January 2019 | work = [[Deadline Hollywood]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190111205330/https://deadline.com/2019/01/netflixs-black-mirror-bandersnatch-subject-of-suit-over-use-of-choose-your-own-adventure-1202533643/ | archive-date = 11 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-sued-exploiting-choose-your-own-adventure-black-mirror-bandersnatch-1175428 | title = Netflix's 'Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Leads to "Choose Your Own Adventure" Trademark Lawsuit | first = Eriq | last = Gardner | date = 11 January 2019 | access-date = 11 January 2019 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190111205130/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-sued-exploiting-choose-your-own-adventure-black-mirror-bandersnatch-1175428 | archive-date = 11 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref> Netflix sought to have the suit summarily dismissed on a number of grounds related to trademark law and fair use allowances, but this was denied by the presiding judge based on evidence brought by Chooseco, the full case scheduled to proceed by February 2020.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-asks-judge-dismiss-choose-your-own-adventure-lawsuit-1196317 | title = Netflix Asks Judge to Dismiss "Choose Your Own Adventure" Lawsuit | first = Eriq | last = Gardner | date = 21 March 2019 | access-date = 22 March 2019 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190322144634/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-asks-judge-dismiss-choose-your-own-adventure-lawsuit-1196317 | archive-date = 22 March 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/netflix-cant-escape-choose-your-own-adventure-trademark-suit | title = Netflix Can't Escape 'Choose Your Own Adventure' Trademark Suit | first = Blake | last = Brittian | date = 12 February 2020 | access-date = 23 February 2020 | work = [[Bloomberg Law]] | url-access = subscription | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200223223910/https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/netflix-cant-escape-choose-your-own-adventure-trademark-suit | archive-date = 23 February 2020 | url-status = live }}</ref> Netflix continued to seek dismissal, arguing that the "choose your own adventure" term had fallen into a [[generic trademark]], and that the branch of the story where it shows Stefan being controlled by a person watching Netflix makes the work different from past "Choose Your Own Adventure" books which put the reader into the role of the protagonist.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-seeks-cancellation-choose-your-own-adventure-trademark-bandersnatch-dispute-1281305 | title = Netflix Seeks Cancellation of "Choose Your Own Adventure" Trademark in 'Bandersnatch' Dispute | date = 26 February 2020 | access-date = 27 February 2020 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200226180820/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-seeks-cancellation-choose-your-own-adventure-trademark-bandersnatch-dispute-1281305 | archive-date = 26 February 2020 | url-status = live }}</ref> In November 2020, Netflix and Chooseco reached a settlement, the terms of which were not disclosed.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-chooses-settlement-to-end-trademark-lawsuit-over-black-mirror | title = Netflix Chooses Settlement to End Trademark Lawsuit Over 'Black Mirror' | date = 24 November 2020 | access-date = 25 November 2020 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-date = 24 November 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201124204518/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/netflix-chooses-settlement-to-end-trademark-lawsuit-over-black-mirror | url-status = live }}</ref>

==Analysis==
A 1980s period piece and a work of [[science fiction]], ''Bandersnatch'' also contains elements of [[comedy]], [[Horror film|horror]] and [[pathos]]. It has been described as a [[psychological thriller]].<ref name="wired"/><ref name="iw"/><ref name="cnn"/> The film heavily incorporates ideas of [[postmodernism]], containing meta-commentary and an [[unreliable narrator]], with [[free will]] as a central theme.<ref name="iw">{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-groundbreaking-interactive-fun-netflix-spoilers-1202031049/ |title='Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Review: Groundbreaking Choose-Your-Own Adventure Storytelling |work=[[IndieWire]] |last=Miller |first=Liz Shannon |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228183614/https://www.indiewire.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-groundbreaking-interactive-fun-netflix-spoilers-1202031049/ |archive-date=28 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="salon"/><ref name="SMH"/> Ed Cumming of ''[[The Independent]]'' commented that it contains themes of "authorial control, free will and fate".<ref name="indy review">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-netflix-interactive-episode-movie-ending-release-stream-a8701831.html |title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch, review – Charlie Brooker's intriguing but imperfect postmodern adventure |work=[[The Independent]] |last=Cumming |first=Ed |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=21 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323230205/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-netflix-interactive-episode-movie-ending-release-stream-a8701831.html |archive-date=23 March 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> Beth Elderkin of ''[[io9]]'' wrote that ''Bandersnatch'' is about the absence of choice, and Stefan's life being outside of his control. Elderkin highlighted the "White Rabbit" ending, in which Stefan finds his rabbit under his bed as a child and joins his mother in dying on the train, as the one point where "free will is celebrated instead of derided".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/the-hidden-beauty-of-black-mirror-bandersnatchs-best-e-1831369911|title=The Hidden Beauty of ''Black Mirror'': ''Bandersnatch''{{'}}s Best Ending|work=[[io9]]|publisher=[[Gawker Media]]|last=Elderkin|first=Beth|date=31 December 2018|access-date=1 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181231230911/https://io9.gizmodo.com/the-hidden-beauty-of-black-mirror-bandersnatchs-best-e-1831369911|archive-date=31 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> These ideas and themes of monitoring and control, as well as the 1984 setting, led to comparisons to [[George Orwell]]'s novel ''[[Nineteen Eighty-Four]]''.<ref name="thr allusions"/><ref name="vox allusions">{{cite web |url=https://www.vox.com/culture/2018/12/28/18158908/black-mirror-bandersnatch-1984-no-spoilers-netflix-data |title=3 non-spoilery things to know before you watch Black Mirror: Bandersnatch |first=Alissa |last=Wilkerson |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |work=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228232637/https://www.vox.com/culture/2018/12/28/18158908/black-mirror-bandersnatch-1984-no-spoilers-netflix-data |archive-date=28 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> Stuart Heritage of ''[[The Guardian]]'' wrote that "Brooker has popularised a new form of storytelling, then identified its [[trope (cinema)|tropes]] and dismantled them one by one."<ref name="guardian"/>

The work was compared to a wide variety of media. Keith Spencer of ''[[Salon (website)|Salon]]'' made comparisons to early internet-era [[hypertext fiction]] and the previous Netflix interactive work ''Puss in Book'', which has a broadly similar plot of a character being driven mad by the knowledge that they are controlled by an external force.<ref name="salon"/> David Griffin of ''[[IGN]]'' compared it to the adventure video game series ''[[The Walking Dead (video game series)|The Walking Dead]]'', whose first installment was released in 2012, and the 2018 adventure game ''[[Detroit: Become Human]]''.<ref name="ign"/> Karl Quinn of ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'' compared the work to ''[[Mosaic (murder mystery)|Mosaic]]'', a 2017 murder mystery released by [[HBO]] as an interactive app.<ref name="SMH"/> Brooker also compared the story to the 1993 comedy fantasy ''[[Groundhog Day (film)|Groundhog Day]]'', about a character who re-lives the same day repeatedly.<ref name="independent">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/features/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-interactive-charlie-brooker-interview-a8701626.html |title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch is an experiment on us – Netflix explain why interactive episode is the grimmest yet |work=[[The Independent]] |last=Streitfeld |first=David |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190101135403/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/features/black-mirror-bandersnatch-netflix-interactive-charlie-brooker-interview-a8701626.html |archive-date=1 January 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Burroughs1983_crop_b.jpg|thumb|right|upright|alt=William S. Burroughs|One critic drew connections between the character Jerome F. Davies and the postmodern writer [[William S. Burroughs]] ''(pictured)''.<ref name="thr allusions"/>]]
The term "[[bandersnatch]]" originates from a fictional creature created by [[Lewis Carroll]], which appears in his 1870s poems "[[Jabberwocky]]" and "[[The Hunting of the Snark]]". The former appears in the novel ''[[Through the Looking-Glass]]'', the sequel to ''[[Alice's Adventures in Wonderland]]''.<ref name="thr allusions">{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-bandersnatch-real-life-works-influences-1173330 | title = 'Bandersnatch': The Works That Inspired the 'Black Mirror' Interactive Feature | first = Rosie | last = Knight | date = 4 January 2019 | access-date = 4 January 2019 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190105035401/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-bandersnatch-real-life-works-influences-1173330 | archive-date = 5 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-bandersnatch-what-is-a-bandersnatch-lewis-carroll-through-the-looking-glass/ |title='Black Mirror': So What Is a Bandersnatch, Anyway? |work=[[TheWrap]] |last=Maas |first=Jennifer |date=26 December 2018 |access-date=27 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181227044441/https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-bandersnatch-what-is-a-bandersnatch-lewis-carroll-through-the-looking-glass/ |archive-date=27 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> A planned video game by [[Imagine Software]], ''[[Bandersnatch (video game)|Bandersnatch]]'', took its name from the creature.<ref name="thr allusions"/> Its name was mentioned in an [[Easter egg (media)|Easter egg]] in series three episode "Playtest", on the front cover of a magazine which is briefly shown onscreen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/netflix-black-mirror-season-5-premiere-date-choose-your-own-adventure/ |title=Netflix's ''Black Mirror'' Leak Has the Fan Theories Flowing Already |work=[[TV Guide]] |last=Bell |first=Amanda |date=2 December 2018 |access-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228083356/https://www.tvguide.com/news/netflix-black-mirror-season-5-premiere-date-choose-your-own-adventure/ |archive-date=28 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> One of several expensive "megagames" which Imagine Software worked on, ''Bandersnatch'' was never released as the company went bankrupt in 1984. Imagine's closure was widely publicised because of the [[BBC]]'s "Commercial Breaks" series which followed the company's closure and its cascading effects on the British video game industry.<ref name="telegraph speculation"/> As an allusion, the film opens on 9 July 1984, the day Imagine Software closed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2019-09-06/black-mirror-bandersnatch-whats-it-about-whos-in-the-cast-and-can-i-watch-it-on-netflix/|title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch – What's it about, who's in the cast and can I watch it on Netflix?|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Chapman|first=Tom|date=6 September 2019|access-date=20 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604194544/https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2019-09-06/black-mirror-bandersnatch-whats-it-about-whos-in-the-cast-and-can-i-watch-it-on-netflix/|archive-date=4 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

The story shares elements of the works of [[Philip K. Dick]], who frequently wrote about alternate realities and timelines. Jerome F. Davies—the archetype of a [[tortured artist]]—can be seen as an allusion to Dick, who frequently used recreational drugs throughout his life, and at one point attempted to kill his wife.<ref name="thr allusions"/><ref name="slate dick">{{cite web | url = https://slate.com/culture/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-endings-spoilers.html | title = Here Are All the Endings to Black Mirror's Interactive Episode, "Bandersnatch" | first = Sam | last = Adams | date = 28 December 2018 | access-date = 31 December 2018 | work = [[Slate (magazine)|Slate]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181230115924/https://slate.com/culture/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-endings-spoilers.html | archive-date = 30 December 2018 | url-status = live }}</ref> The original book cover of Dick's ''[[Ubik]]'' is prominently featured in Colin's apartment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/black-mirror-bandersnatch-and-its-philip-k-dick-influences/|title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch and Its Philip K. Dick Influences|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Britt|first=Ryan|date=7 January 2019|access-date=21 June 2020|archive-date=21 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421155523/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/black-mirror-bandersnatch-and-its-philip-k-dick-influences/|url-status=live}}</ref> Rosie Knight of ''The Hollywood Reporter'' compared Davies to writer [[William S. Burroughs]], who killed his second wife.<ref name="thr allusions"/> In ''Bandersnatch'', there is no ending in which Stefan is happy and the game gets a good review. Jackson McHenry of ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]'' wrote that this implied "a link between mental illness, violence, and creativity". Brooker responded that the game itself could be "a force of evil" and said that "the less friction there is in Stefan's life, the more boring the story for an onlooker becomes".<ref name="Vulture interview"/>

===Easter eggs===
[[File:White Bear Black Mirror.svg|thumb|upright=0.75|alt=white shape on black background|The [[glyph]] from "[[White Bear (Black Mirror)|White Bear]]" reappears in ''Bandersnatch'' representing two branching pathways.]]
Like previous instalments of ''Black Mirror'', ''Bandersnatch'' makes allusions to earlier episodes.<ref name="thr Easter">{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/bandersnatch-tuckersoft-black-mirror-universe-1172028 | title = How 'Bandersnatch' Fits Into the 'Black Mirror' Universe | first = Jackie | last = Strause | date = 31 December 2018 | access-date = 2 January 2019 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190102053516/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/bandersnatch-tuckersoft-black-mirror-universe-1172028 | archive-date = 2 January 2019 | url-status = live }}</ref> The "branching path" symbol which Davies and later Butler experience is a motif from the series two episode "[[White Bear (Black Mirror)|White Bear]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-bandersnatch-trailer-metalhead-white-bear-video/ |title='Bandersnatch' Trailer Sneaks in Shout-Outs to Past 'Black Mirror' Favorites (Video) |first=Jennifer |last=Maas |date=27 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |work=[[The Wrap]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228030914/https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-bandersnatch-trailer-metalhead-white-bear-video/ |archive-date=28 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> One of Tuckersoft's games is ''Metl Hedd'', a reference to "Metalhead", while Ritman is shown to be working on a game called ''Nohzdyve'', referencing the episode "[[Nosedive (Black Mirror)|Nosedive]]".<ref name="vulture egg"/> Butler attends counselling at the Saint Juniper clinic, named after "[[San Junipero]]".<ref name="indy review"/><ref name="vulture egg"/> References to a wide range of events associated with other ''Black Mirror'' episodes can be seen in news stories shown in brief shots of the pages of ''[[The Sun (United Kingdom)|The Sun]]'' newspaper and on a television news crawl.<ref name="vulture egg">{{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-easter-eggs.html |title=All the Black Mirror Easter Eggs Hidden in Bandersnatch |first=Brian |last=Tallrico |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181231073857/https://www.vulture.com/2018/12/black-mirror-bandersnatch-easter-eggs.html |archive-date=31 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="wrap egg">{{cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/bandersnatch-black-mirror-references-uss-callister-tuckersoft-tckr-systems/ |title=Here Are All the References We've Found That Tie 'Bandersnatch' to the Rest of 'Black Mirror' Universe |first1=Jennifer |last1=Maas |first2=Phil |last2=Owen |first3=Tim |last3=Baysinger |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2018 |work=[[The Wrap]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229011745/https://www.thewrap.com/bandersnatch-black-mirror-references-uss-callister-tuckersoft-tckr-systems/ |archive-date=29 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> The character Dr. R. Haynes alludes to Rolo Haynes, the proprietor of the titular showcase in "[[Black Museum (Black Mirror)|Black Museum]]".<ref name="vulture egg"/><ref name="wrap egg"/> There are also Easter eggs to series five episodes which were yet to be released, such as the mention of "[[Smithereens (Black Mirror)|Smithereens]]" character Billy Bauer in a news ticker.<ref name="dog interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-bandersnatch-interview-we-all-had-our-stefan-moment/|title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch interview – 'We all had our Stefan moment'|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Mellor|first=Louisa|date=14 January 2019|access-date=15 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114144741/https://www.denofgeek.com/uk/tv/black-mirror/62710/black-mirror-bandersnatch-interview-we-all-had-our-stefan-moment|archive-date=14 January 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="indy">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-5-smithereens-review-andrew-scott-netflix-charlie-brooker-a8943576.html|title=Black Mirror, season 5, 'Smithereens' review: A thin premise that doesn't justify the running time|work=[[The Independent]]|publisher=Independent Print Limited|last=Cumming|first=Ed|date=5 June 2019|access-date=5 June 2019|archive-date=5 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605092624/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-5-smithereens-review-andrew-scott-netflix-charlie-brooker-a8943576.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Brooker, Slade and McLean discussed whether there was deeper meaning in the Easter eggs. Slade was reluctant to include the ''Metl Hedd'' game, not finding "the need for it". Slade commented that Tuckersoft could later have become TCKR, a company in "San Junipero" and thought that "Metalhead" was an event in the future rather than a simulation. McLean said that stories are developed in isolation, rather than by asking "how do we fit the story into this universe?" Brooker saw the Easter eggs as "a nice nod to superfans" which should not affect the creative process or force viewers to watch the stories in a particular order.<ref name="thr Easter"/> Brooker and Poulter have suggested that the character of Colin Ritman could potentially show up in future ''Black Mirror'' stories, given that the character, in certain paths, seems to just disappear but has awareness of alternate timelines and realities;<ref name="thr s5"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/black-mirror-will-poulter-details-time-travel-idea-for-bandersnatch-sequel-2705304|title='Black Mirror': Will Poulter details "time travel" idea for 'Bandersnatch' sequel|work=[[NME]]|last=Krol|first=Charlotte|date=10 July 2020|access-date=14 July 2020|archive-date=13 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713184328/https://www.nme.com/news/tv/black-mirror-will-poulter-details-time-travel-idea-for-bandersnatch-sequel-2705304|url-status=live}}</ref> he reappeared in season 7's "[[Plaything (Black Mirror)|Plaything]]".

In one ending, the sound of a computer data tape recording is heard; loading the sound into a ZX Spectrum generates a [[QR code]] with the White Bear [[glyph]] in the middle that leads to the fictional Tuckersoft website, where a playable copy of the ZX Spectrum game ''Nohzdyve'' can be downloaded.<ref name="verge game">{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/12/28/18159196/black-mirror-bandersnatch-nohzdyve-play-emulator |title=One of Black Mirror: Bandersnatch's games is available to play right now |first=Julia |last=Alexander |date=28 December 2018 |website=[[The Verge]] |access-date=21 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611231420/https://www.theverge.com/2018/12/28/18159196/black-mirror-bandersnatch-nohzdyve-play-emulator |archive-date=11 June 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/bandersnatchs-stockpile-of-black-mirror-easter-eggs-inc-1831365758|title=''Bandersnatch''{{'}}s stockpile of ''Black'' Mirror Easter eggs includes a playable video game take on an old episode|last=Hughes|first=William|date=28 December 2018|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=28 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229012021/https://news.avclub.com/bandersnatchs-stockpile-of-black-mirror-easter-eggs-inc-1831365758|archive-date=29 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> This ending was at one point intended to be a clue to a real life treasure hunt in which people could find ''Bandersnatch'' cassettes, inspired by the 1979 picture book ''[[Masquerade (book)|Masquerade]]'' that gave hints as to the location of a buried bejewelled golden hare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/charlie-brooker-we-planned-a-worldwide-bandersnatch-treasure-hunt|title=Charlie Brooker: We planned a worldwide Bandersnatch treasure hunt|work=[[GQ]]|last=McGurk|first=Stuart|date=11 January 2019|access-date=3 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702224417/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/charlie-brooker-we-planned-a-worldwide-bandersnatch-treasure-hunt|archive-date=2 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==
On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 74% of 72 reviews are positive for the film, with an average rating of 7.5/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "While ''Bandersnatch'' marks an innovative step forward for interactive content, its meta narrative can't quite sustain interest over multiple viewings — though it provides enough trademark ''Black Mirror'' tech horror to warrant at least one watch."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/black_mirror/s04.1 |title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch |access-date=9 November 2019 |publisher=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328224829/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/black_mirror/52530 |archive-date=28 March 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> According to [[Metacritic]], the film received "generally favorable reviews" based on a weighted average score of 61 out of 100 from 16 critic reviews.<ref>{{cite web |title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/black-mirror-bandersnatch |website=Metacritic |access-date=2023-07-20}}</ref> It garnered ratings of four out of five stars in ''The Independent'' and ''[[The Observer]]'', and three stars in ''[[Rolling Stone]]''.<ref name="indy review"/><ref name="observer"/><ref name="stone">{{cite magazine | url = https://www.rollingstone.com/tv/tv-reviews/black-mirror-bandersnatch-tv-review-772876/ | title = 'Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Review: Choose Your Own Delirium, Disappointment | first = David | last = Fear | date = 30 December 2018 | access-date = 21 June 2020 | magazine = [[Rolling Stone]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200603210710/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv/tv-reviews/black-mirror-bandersnatch-tv-review-772876/ | archive-date = 3 June 2020 | url-status = live }}</ref> ''[[IndieWire]]'' gave it an A− rating and ''IGN'' reviewed it as eight out of ten.<ref name="ign">{{cite web |url=https://ign.com/articles/2018/12/28/netflixs-black-mirror-bandersnatch-review |title=Netflix's Black Mirror: Bandersnatch Review |work=[[IGN]] |last=Griffin |first=David |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=21 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181231175231/https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/12/28/netflixs-black-mirror-bandersnatch-review |archive-date=31 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="iw"/>

Describing the piece as "incredibly funny at times", Heritage reviewed it as a "masterpiece of sophistication".<ref name="guardian">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2018/dec/28/black-mirrors-bandersnatch-charlie-brookers-meta-masterpiece |title=Black Mirror's Bandersnatch: Charlie Brooker's meta masterpiece |work=[[The Guardian]] |last=Heritage |first=Stuart |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=21 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617215411/https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2018/dec/28/black-mirrors-bandersnatch-charlie-brookers-meta-masterpiece |archive-date=17 June 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> Liz Shannon Miller of ''IndieWire'' found it "hard-to-define" but "impossible to forget".<ref name="iw"/> Quinn believed it to be one of the better instalments of ''Black Mirror'', saying that it was a "brilliant foray into a (more or less) new realm of visual storytelling".<ref name="SMH">{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/bandersnatch-the-netflix-show-everyone-is-talking-about-but-is-it-any-good-20190101-p50p3i.html|title=Bandersnatch: The Netflix show everyone is talking about, but is it any good?|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|last=Quinn|first=Karl|date=1 January 2019|access-date=2 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221095623/https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/bandersnatch-the-netflix-show-everyone-is-talking-about-but-is-it-any-good-20190101-p50p3i.html|archive-date=21 February 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> However, Brian Lowry of [[CNN]] wrote that it was "a wildly familiar plot for a psychological thriller" and Spencer said that the storyline "isn't particularly memorable".<ref name="cnn">{{cite web |url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/12/28/entertainment/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review/index.html |title='Black Mirror' plays gimmicky game with 'Bandersnatch' |first=Brian |last=Lowry |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=21 June 2020 |publisher=[[CNN]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514164701/https://www.cnn.com/2018/12/28/entertainment/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review/index.html |archive-date=14 May 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="salon">{{cite web|url=https://www.salon.com/2019/01/01/mired-in-self-referential-cliche-bandersnatch-cant-transcend-its-form/|title=Mired in self-referential cliche, "Bandersnatch" can't transcend its form|work=[[Salon (website)|Salon]]|last=Spencer|first=Keith A.|date=1 January 2019|access-date=2 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514230939/https://www.salon.com/2019/01/01/mired-in-self-referential-cliche-bandersnatch-cant-transcend-its-form/|archive-date=14 May 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Austen Goslin of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' criticised that the narrative is "like a cleverly disguised straight line".<ref name="polygon">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/12/28/18159087/netflix-black-mirror-bandersnatch-interactive-film-game|title=Black Mirror: Bandersnatch is fun, but doesn't quite work as a movie or a game|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|last=Goslin|first=Austen|date=28 December 2018|access-date=2 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604193503/https://www.polygon.com/2018/12/28/18159087/netflix-black-mirror-bandersnatch-interactive-film-game|archive-date=4 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

The technical design of ''Bandersnatch'' was widely praised. Griffin wrote that the tutorial "does a solid job of explaining how the experience works".<ref name="ign"/> The user interface and transitions between choice points were lauded by critics including Heritage and ''[[NPR]]''{{'}}s Linda Holmes, who both called it "seamless", and Griffin, who found the feature "smooth and unobtrusive".<ref name="ign"/><ref name="guardian"/><ref name="npr">{{cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/2018/12/28/680671691/black-mirror-bandersnatch-makes-you-choose-your-own-adventure |title='Black Mirror: Bandersnatch' Makes You Choose Your Own Adventure |first=Linda |last=Holmes |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=2 June 2020 |work=[[NPR]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514052440/https://www.npr.org/2018/12/28/680671691/black-mirror-bandersnatch-makes-you-choose-your-own-adventure |archive-date=14 May 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> Miller commented that "the system was very smart about knowing when to essentially fast-forward through earlier storylines to move things forward".<ref name="iw"/> The relationship between interactivity and the storyline, however, received less positive reception. Griffin reviewed that the "short amount of time" to make a choice could cause frustration.<ref name="ign"/> Goslin believed that the interactivity leads to "staccato pacing that prevents anyone involved from finding a real rhythm in each scene", Roisin O'Connor of ''The Independent'' concurring that the choices "can become quite wearisome".<ref name="O'Connor">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/bandersnatch-live-updates-black-mirror-netfix-latest-decisions-endings-interactive-stefan-choices-a8701701.html |title=What happened when we watched the Black Mirror film, Bandersnatch |work=[[The Independent]] |last=O'Connor |first=Roisin |date=28 December 2018 |access-date=2 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228194315/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/bandersnatch-live-updates-black-mirror-netfix-latest-decisions-endings-interactive-stefan-choices-a8701701.html |archive-date=28 December 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="polygon"/> Lowry said that the medium "winds up feeling like a gimmick".<ref name="cnn"/>

The narrative received further criticism. Spencer found it "riddled with cliche", saying that Stefan questioning the nature of free will "has been done to death in print" and other interactive fiction.<ref name="salon"/> Holmes wrote that "it would have been good to see this technology demonstrated on a stronger story".<ref name="npr"/> Lowry found that the story kept "circling back", which was "numbing and repetitive".<ref name="cnn"/> Holmes agreed, finding it "deeply frustrating" when she was "simply shown the same segment of story again" until she made the choice "that will actually move you forward".<ref name="npr"/> Lucy Mangan of ''The Observer'' experienced that the story "rarely landed in an unexpected place".<ref name="observer">{{cite web | url = https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2019/jan/01/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-charlie-brooker-netflix-tv-of-tomorrow-is-now-here | title = Black Mirror: Bandersnatch review – the TV of tomorrow is now here | first = Lucy | last = Mangan | date = 31 December 2018 | access-date = 2 June 2020 | work = [[The Observer]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200527215655/https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2019/jan/01/black-mirror-bandersnatch-review-charlie-brooker-netflix-tv-of-tomorrow-is-now-here | archive-date = 27 May 2020 | url-status = live }}</ref> Overall, ''Rolling Stone''{{'}}s David Fear criticised that the experience gave "little to hold onto after the fact" and that "the story doesn't matter".<ref name="stone"/> Holmes found it "especially poorly suited to being watched more than once".<ref name="npr"/> In contrast, Cumming reviewed that the medium "is bound with the plot", which "saves the film from pure gimmickry".<ref name="indy review"/> Griffin felt "responsible" for Stefan's behaviour and "more and more invested in his story".<ref name="ign"/> Miller and Quinn both praised the self-referential "Netflix" branch of the story.<ref name="iw"/><ref name="SMH"/>

The characters were met with mostly negative commentary. Goslin called them "paper thin and barely interesting"; Mangan wrote that the medium did not have "energy to spare to make the characters much more than ciphers".<ref name="observer"/><ref name="polygon"/> Holmes criticised that the "isolated artist" trope "doesn't really hold up a narrative on its own". She further said that the audience doesn't "learn enough about who [Stefan] is to care about him".<ref name="npr"/> In regard to Stefan's backstory involving his mother's death, Goslin commented that ''Bandersnatch'' is "really only interested in this premise as a bridge toward its ultimate destination: becoming meta commentary on itself and video games as a medium".<ref name="polygon"/> However, the acting was met with praise from Griffin, who approved of "impactful performances from Fionn Whitehead and Will Poulter", and Cumming, finding that Poulter "steals most of his scenes".<ref name="ign"/><ref name="indy review"/> Cumming further wrote that "the dialogue is as knowing and smart as we have come to expect".<ref name="indy review"/>

===Episode rankings===
''Bandersnatch'' received mixed rankings on critics' lists of the 23 instalments of ''Black Mirror'', from best to worst:
{{col-begin}}
{{col-2}}
* 5th (of the Top Seven) – Al Horner, ''[[GQ]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/gallery/best-black-mirror-episodes|title=The best Black Mirror episodes of all time|work=[[GQ]]|last=Horner|first=Al|date=6 June 2019|access-date=3 January 2021|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702224405/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/gallery/best-black-mirror-episodes|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 5th – Ed Power, ''The Telegraph''<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-every-episode-ranked-rated/|title=Black Mirror: every episode ranked and rated, from Striking Vipers to San Junipero|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=28 December 2017|access-date=21 June 2020|url-access=limited|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101030556/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-every-episode-ranked-rated/|archive-date=1 January 2018}}</ref>
* 6th – Matt Donnelly and Tim Molloy, ''[[TheWrap]]''<ref name="wrap ranking">{{cite web | url=https://www.thewrap.com/all-19-black-mirror-episodes-ranked-from-good-to-mind-blowing-photos/ | title='Striking Vipers' to 'National Anthem': Every 'Black Mirror' Ranked, From Good to Mind-Blowing (Photos) | author=Donnelly, Matt | author2=Molloy, Tim | website=[[TheWrap]] | access-date=21 June 2020 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180217192830/https://www.thewrap.com/all-19-black-mirror-episodes-ranked-from-good-to-mind-blowing-photos/ | archive-date=17 February 2018 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>
* 11th – Charles Bramesco, ''Vulture''<ref name="vulture ranking">{{cite web | url=http://www.vulture.com/2016/10/every-black-mirror-episode-from-worst-to-best.html | title=Every ''Black Mirror'' Episode, Ranked | author=Bramesco, Charles | date=21 October 2016 | website=[[Vulture.com|Vulture]] | access-date=21 June 2020 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312082859/http://www.vulture.com/2016/10/every-black-mirror-episode-from-worst-to-best.html | archive-date=12 March 2018 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

===Awards===
{{See also|List of awards and nominations received by Black Mirror {{!}} List of awards and nominations received by ''Black Mirror''}}
Among its nominations, ''Bandersnatch'' won two [[Primetime Emmy Award]]s and a [[Broadcasting Press Guild]] TV and Radio Award in the Innovation category.<ref name="innovation"/> Charlie Brooker won the Best Game Writing category at the 2018 [[Nebula Awards]] in 2019, rather than a storytelling category.<ref name="nebula"/>
